<reason>B won by keeping the written motion intact: unmapped seafloor is a coverage problem for cheap machines, not a warrant for space-scale crewed programmes. A’s trap—either crewed exploration is worth a premium (so fund the nearer, load-bearing abyss) or cut space until parity arrives—was sharp, but B answered it without collapsing: different products, sequenceable from a dock, postage-stamp hulls. A’s honest “yes” to still demanding NASA-scale crewed funding after a finished map let B treat the given clause as pretext and made A’s later “value returned” close look like a different motion. A remaining live routes (capacity gap, industrial-base-with-crews-at-centre) were answered as reasons to keep a handful of hulls, not to match a space agency. A’s clipped opening and space-deletion close were clever but did not recapture the decision rule.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Q1 plus B4.5–B4.8: A’s admission that mapped seafloor would still require space-comparable crewed funding turned “unmapped” into atmosphere, after which B could weigh method and centre of gravity against the motion as written.</best_rebuttal>
